fields.questionText: The balanced chemical equation showing the reaction between quicklime and water is:
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option is (c). Quicklime (CaO) reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime, calcium hydroxide, releasing heat: CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq) + Heat. No H2 or O2 is formed, and the equation is balanced (Ca 1, O 2, H 2 on each side).

rationale: Restored lost reaction arrows in options/answer; replaced mark-scheme residue 'c) 1 1' with proper answer and justification. Correct option (c) unchanged in substance.

fields.questionText: Study the following chemical reaction: 2Na(s) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H2(g). The reducing agent in this reaction is:
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option is (a) Na. Sodium reduces water to hydrogen gas (H2O loses oxygen/H is released) while sodium itself is oxidised to NaOH; the substance that gets oxidised and reduces another is the reducing agent.

rationale: Restored the lost arrow in the equation; replaced residue 'a) 1 1' with answer + justification; specific subtopic. Answer Na unchanged.

fields.questionText: A dilute solution of sodium carbonate was added to two test tubes — one containing dilute HCl (test tube A) and the other containing dilute NaOH (test tube B). The correct observation would be:
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option is (c). In test tube A, the acid reacts with sodium carbonate: Na2CO3 + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H2O + CO2; colourless CO2 gas is liberated. In test tube B, NaOH (a base) does not react with sodium carbonate, so no gas is evolved.

rationale: Restored the truncated NCERT Exemplar stem (test tube B = dil NaOH, question line) as implied by options. Topic is acid/base + carbonate reaction, so retagged to acids-bases-and-salts.

fields.questionText: Ethane (C2H6) on complete combustion gives CO2 and water. If the equation is balanced in accordance with the law of conservation of mass, the coefficient of oxygen is equal to:
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option is (d) 7/2. C2H6 + O2 → CO2 + H2O; balance C: 2CO2; balance H: 3H2O; O atoms on right = 4 + 3 = 7, so O2 coefficient = 7/2: C2H6 + 7/2 O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O (i.e. 2C2H6 + 7O2 → 4CO2 + 6H2O).

rationale: Restored garbled formula 'C H 2 6' to C2H6 and tidied stem; added balancing working. Answer 7/2 verified.

fields.questionText: Lead nitrate powder is heated strongly in a dry boiling tube and brown fumes are observed. Identify the product evolved as brown fumes during this reaction.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option is (b). On heating, lead nitrate decomposes: 2Pb(NO3)2(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO2(g) + O2(g). The brown fumes are of nitrogen dioxide (NO2); oxygen is colourless.

rationale: Stem pointed to an unshown 'above reaction'; the row's own diagramDescription/solution confirm it is heating of lead nitrate, so context is written into the stem. Option letter prefixes removed. Answer (b) unchanged.

Fe2O3 is reduced to Fe, and CO is oxidised to CO2.
Both Fe2O3 and CO are reduced to Fe and CO2, respectively.
fields.answer: Fe2O3 is reduced to Fe, and CO is oxidised to CO2.
fields.finalAnswer: (c) Fe2O3 is reduced to Fe, and CO is oxidised to CO2.

fields.questionText: Write the essential condition for the following reaction to take place: 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br2. Write one application of this reaction.

[1 mark] Application: this reaction is used in black and white photography.

fields.questionText: Name the reducing agent in the following reaction: 3MnO2 + 4Al → 3Mn + 2Al2O3. State which is more reactive, Mn or Al, and why?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Al is the reducing agent — it removes oxygen from MnO2 (reducing it to Mn) and is itself oxidised to Al2O3.
[1 mark] Al is more reactive than Mn because Al displaces Mn from its compound MnO2.

rationale: Fixed stray '$' to arrow, '4A1' to 4Al, and balanced Al2O3 (coefficient 2); split solution into 1+1 steps. Answer unchanged.

fields.questionText: A single displacement reaction is represented below: PQ + R → PR + Q. Which of the following is true about the reactants and products?
options: R forms the cation in the product, and PR is more stable than PQ.
R forms the cation in the product, and PR is less stable than PQ.
R forms the anion in the product, and PR is more stable than PQ.
R forms the anion in the product, and PR is less stable than PQ.
fields.answer: R forms the anion in the product, and PR is more stable than PQ.
fields.finalAnswer: (c) R forms the anion in the product, and PR is more stable than PQ.

rationale: Option texts were inline in the stem with bare labels A-D as options; moved them into the options array. Answer (c) unchanged (R replaces anion Q; displacement occurs only if PR is more stable).

fields.questionText: Write the chemical equation for each of the following: (i) Combustion of methane (ii) Oxidation of ethanol (iii) Hydrogenation of ethene (iv) Esterification reaction (v) Saponification reaction
fields.answer: (i) CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + heat (ii) CH3CH2OH →(alkaline KMnO4, heat) CH3COOH (iii) CH2=CH2 + H2 →(Ni catalyst) CH3–CH3 (iv) CH3COOH + C2H5OH →(conc. H2SO4) CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (v) CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) Combustion of methane: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + heat and light.
[1 mark] (ii) Oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid: CH3CH2OH →(alkaline KMnO4, heat / acidified K2Cr2O7) CH3COOH.
[1 mark] (iii) Hydrogenation of ethene: CH2=CH2 + H2 →(Ni catalyst) CH3–CH3 (ethane).
[1 mark] (iv) Esterification: CH3COOH + C2H5OH →(conc. H2SO4, warm) CH3COOC2H5 (ethyl ethanoate) + H2O.
[1 mark] (v) Saponification: CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH.
fields.finalAnswer: (i) CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O (ii) CH3CH2OH → CH3COOH (alkaline KMnO4/heat) (iii) CH2=CH2 + H2 → CH3–CH3 (Ni) (iv) CH3COOH + C2H5OH → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (conc. H2SO4) (v) CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH

rationale: Removed 'SECTION – E' header and '5' mark residues; dropped OR-(B) whose (iv)(a) structure is missing (figure). Kept self-contained 5-mark (A). All carbon-compound reactions: retagged carbon-and-its-compounds.
